newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures fell on Friday, after stronger-than-expected US data rattled bond markets worldwide, but outperformed both US and German bonds as benign French inflation and favourable EMU comments sparked investor interest in cash bonds at the long end of the curve.
Both 10- and 30-year OATs outperformed Bunds, the spreads widening slightly to minus 15 and minus eight basis points and the gap between US 10-year bonds moved as high as 128.
The sense that investors would support the French market, even though flows were fairly sparse helped limit the decline in the June bond future, analysts said.

"The French market's had a good run for its money against the German market in the past few days. We've had encouraging words (about monetary union), even from Germany itself," Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais said.

"France is also doing better than German in this downdraft with US Treasuries, which is a feature we always thought we'd see. Overall we've got a sense that this week has been a confidence building exercise," he said.
"The March finished goods PPI came out about as expected but the 'core' PPI rose by a strong 0.4 percent," Nathalie Benatia economist at Banque Nationale de Paris, said.
The June bond future tumbled from near the day's high of 128.56 to a session low of 128.08 after a stronger-than-expected rise in March US producer prices, excluding food and energy.

Traders said there was continued interest in the very long end of the curve, notably in 30-year principal strips although as much of the value in franc bonds has now been squeezed out some investors were looking at the Ecu strips instead.

Nathalie Fillet, bond analyst at Banque Paribas said however that if the US bond future fell back to 106, which was on the cards as it slumped through key technical levels, the French bond future could drop as low as 127.50.
June PIBOR outperformed Euromarks as the franc climbed further against the mark, reaching 3.3627, the highest level it has been since June 1993.

The interest rate future climbed one basis point to 96.67, reversing some of Thursday's losses on disappointment the Bank of France had not capitalised on the franc strength to trim its key intervention rate from 3.10 percent.
Adding to support for the French market was a scant 0.1 percent rise in French consumer prices for March, bringing the year-on-year increase to 1.1 percent.
